topics.topic: Scope, required contents, and conditions of the next-backup inclusion guarantee for concurrent committed changes
questions: What does “is in the next” require when the committed change is superseded or erased before the next backup, or when the next run is missed or fails: must the next snapshot preserve that historical result, must only its audit entry remain, or is the promise conditional on the result still existing and a backup being kept?
Does the promise that a concurrent committed change is in the next backup exclude changes to AgentSession records, which backups deliberately never contain?
What exactly must a later backup contain when a transaction commits during a copy, and under what conditions does the assertion “is in the next” apply?

Which changes does the promise “is in the next” cover, and what exactly must a later backup contain when the changed state is deliberately excluded from backups or is changed again before the next snapshot?

quotes:
Its read transaction
   and the store's writes do not wait for each other: a change committed
   while the copy is made goes on, is not in this backup and is in the
   next, and no change or run is refused or fails for the other.

A backup holds every record but the agent sessions (M06), which are
   removed from the copy before it is encrypted, so the copy is a store of
   its own that passes the same checks; Registry's other invariants are not
   checked again in it, its transactions having kept them: a store restored
   from it has no session, Kernel registers its sessions again and the owner
   grants them again, so a restore never brings back a grant revoked after
   the backup.
judgement.divergence: For a grant committed during a backup copy, the first passage requires the next backup to contain the committed change, while the second requires every backup to omit the AgentSession and its grant; the owner after restoration and Kernel observe whether the session and grant exist.
judgement.why: The universal next-backup inclusion promise has no exception for AgentSession changes, but the exclusion rule requires those records and grants to be absent from every backup.

witness.initial: A registered agent session S exists with no grant for project P, and a daily backup has begun its read transaction.
events: The owner grants project P to session S while the backup copy is being made, and the grant transaction commits.
The next daily backup run succeeds and keeps a backup.
After losing the store, the owner puts that next backup in its place and Registry starts on it.
outcomes: The next backup contains the committed grant, so restored session S includes project P.
The next backup contains no AgentSession record, so restored Registry contains neither session S nor its grant for project P.
witness.observer: The owner after restoration and Cabinet Kernel when it reads or uses session S.
basis:
The owner's actions on a session — granting, revoking, changing or clearing
   the active project, answering a request, ending the session — state the
   access version the owner saw; a stale one is refused and nothing changes.

Registry has no restore operation (R0-89). A store the owner puts in
   place of a lost one starts as any store (A17 rule 5) — by the release that
   made its backup, or by a later one after that release's own store
   migration — and begins its own history from the backup: numbering
   continues from its last number (A15), and a store without the migration
   closure accepts the import (A16).

topics.topic: Required SQLite journal/concurrency mode and handling of existing stores in other modes
questions: Must startup require or establish a SQLite journal/concurrency mode that permits the A18 behavior, and if so how is an existing store in another accepted mode treated?

quotes:
The one SQLite database (L19) and its connection: opening it for reading and
writing at start, or making a new, empty store of the release's version under
the temporary name and renaming it once complete, after removing a leftover of
that name and no other file (A17 rule 5), and removing a store it made new
when the start then fails at a listener (A17 rule 2); the full integrity check —
`PRAGMA integrity_check` answering `ok`, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` finding
nothing — and the store version check (A17 rule 5), the same check `backups`
asks of a backup's copy.

SQL, which record goes into which row, the transaction and lock mechanics,
the temporary-name dance of a new store, the integrity pragmas.
judgement.why: State 3 assigns opening every accepted existing store and the backup snapshot to the store module while expressly hiding transaction and lock mechanics, so no particular SQLite journal mode is a State 2 rule; the hidden mechanism must satisfy A18's non-waiting behavior without adding a new startup refusal.
